58	#ifdef CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_SEPARATE
59	static void log_separate(FAR const char *log_file)
60	{
61	  struct file fp;
62	
63	  if (file_open(&fp, log_file, (O_WRONLY | O_APPEND | O_CLOEXEC)) < 0)
64	    {
65	      return;
66	    }
67	
68	  file_write(&fp, "\n\n", 2);
69	
70	  file_close(&fp);
71	}

74	#if CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_ROTATIONS > 0
75	static void log_rotate(FAR const char *log_file)
76	{
77	  int i;
78	  off_t size;
79	  struct stat f_stat;
80	  size_t name_size;
81	  FAR char *rotate_to;
82	  FAR char *rotate_from;
83	
84	  /* Get the size of the current log file. */
85	
86	  if (stat(log_file, &f_stat) < 0)
87	    {
88	      return;
89	    }
90	
91	  size = f_stat.st_size;
92	
93	  /* If it does not exceed the limit we are OK. */
94	
95	  if (size < CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT)
96	    {
97	      return;
98	    }
99	
100	  /* Rotated file names. */
101	
102	  name_size = strlen(log_file) + 8;
103	  rotate_to = kmm_malloc(name_size);
104	  rotate_from = kmm_malloc(name_size);
105	  if ((rotate_to == NULL) || (rotate_from == NULL))
106	    {
107	      goto end;
108	    }
109	
110	  /* Rotate the logs. */
111	
112	  for (i = (CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_ROTATIONS - 1); i > 0; i--)
113	    {
114	      snprintf(rotate_to, name_size, "%s.%d", log_file, i);
115	      snprintf(rotate_from, name_size, "%s.%d", log_file, i - 1);
116	
117	      rename(rotate_from, rotate_to);
118	    }
119	
120	  snprintf(rotate_to, name_size, "%s.0", log_file);
121	
122	  rename(log_file, rotate_to);
123	
124	end:
125	  kmm_free(rotate_to);
126	  kmm_free(rotate_from);
127	}
128	#endif

134	/****************************************************************************
135	 * Name: syslog_file_channel
136	 *
137	 * Description:
138	 *   Configure to use a file in a mounted file system at 'devpath' as the
139	 *   SYSLOG channel.
140	 *
141	 *   This tiny function is simply a wrapper around syslog_dev_initialize()
142	 *   and syslog_channel_register().  It calls syslog_dev_initialize() to
143	 *   configure the character file at 'devpath then calls
144	 *   syslog_channel_register() to use that device as the SYSLOG output
145	 *   channel.
146	 *
147	 *   File SYSLOG channels differ from other SYSLOG channels in that they
148	 *   cannot be established until after fully booting and mounting the target
149	 *   file system.  This function would need to be called from board-specific
150	 *   bring-up logic AFTER mounting the file system containing 'devpath'.
151	 *
152	 *   SYSLOG data generated prior to calling syslog_file_channel will, of
153	 *   course, not be included in the file.
154	 *
155	 *   NOTE interrupt level SYSLOG output will be lost in this case unless
156	 *   the interrupt buffer is used.
157	 *
158	 * Input Parameters:
159	 *   devpath - The full path to the file to be used for SYSLOG output.
160	 *     This may be an existing file or not.  If the file exists,
161	 *     syslog_file_channel() will append new SYSLOG data to the end of the
162	 *     file.  If it does not, then syslog_file_channel() will create the
163	 *     file.
164	 *
165	 * Returned Value:
166	 *   A pointer to the new SYSLOG channel; NULL is returned on any failure.
167	 *
168	 ****************************************************************************/
169	
170	FAR syslog_channel_t *syslog_file_channel(FAR const char *devpath)
171	{
172	  FAR syslog_channel_t *file_channel;
173	
174	  /* Rotate the log file, if needed. */
175	
176	#if CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_ROTATIONS > 0
177	  log_rotate(devpath);
178	#endif
179	
180	  /* Separate the old log entries. */
181	
182	#ifdef CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_SEPARATE
183	  log_separate(devpath);
184	#endif
185	
186	  /* Then initialize the file interface */
187	
188	  file_channel = syslog_dev_initialize(devpath, OPEN_FLAGS, OPEN_MODE);
189	  if (file_channel == NULL)
190	    {
191	      return NULL;
192	    }
193	
194	  /* Use the file as the SYSLOG channel. If this fails we are pretty much
195	   * screwed.
196	   */
197	
198	  if (syslog_channel_register(file_channel) != OK)
199	    {
200	      syslog_dev_uninitialize(file_channel);
201	      file_channel = NULL;
202	    }
203	
204	  return file_channel;
205	}

47	/* The option argument to openlog() is an OR of any of these:
48	 *
49	 *   LOG_CONS     - Write directly to system console if there is an error
50	 *                  while sending to system logger.
51	 *   LOG_NDELAY   - Open the connection immediately (normally, the connection
52	 *                  is opened when the first message is logged).
53	 *   LOG_NOWAIT   - Don't wait for child processes that may have been created
54	 *                  while logging the message.
55	 *   LOG_ODELAY   - The converse of LOG_NDELAY; opening of the connection is
56	 *                  delayed until syslog() is called. (This is the default,
57	 *                  and need not be specified.)
58	 *   LOG_PERROR   - (Not in POSIX.1-2001 or POSIX.1-2008.) Print to stderr
59	 *                  as well (Linux).
60	 *   LOG_PID      - Include PID with each message.
61	 */
62	
63	#define LOG_PID         0x01    /* log the pid with each message */
64	#define LOG_CONS        0x02    /* log on the console if errors in sending */
65	#define LOG_ODELAY      0x04    /* delay open until first syslog() (default) */
66	#define LOG_NDELAY      0x08    /* don't delay open */
67	#define LOG_NOWAIT      0x10    /* don't wait for console forks: DEPRECATED */
68	#define LOG_PERROR      0x20    /* log to stderr as well */
69	
70	/* Note: openlog() is not currently supported */
71	
72	/* The facility argument is used to specify what type of program is logging
73	 * the message. This lets the configuration file specify that messages from
74	 * different facilities will be handled differently.
75	 *
76	 *   LOG_AUTH     - Security/authorization messages
77	 *   LOG_AUTHPRIV - Security/authorization messages (private)
78	 *   LOG_CRON     - Clock daemon (cron and at)
79	 *   LOG_DAEMON   - System daemons without separate facility value
80	 *   LOG_FTP      - FTP daemon
81	 *   LOG_KERN     - Kernel messages (these can't be generated from user
82	 *                  processes)
83	 *   LOG_LOCAL0 through LOG_LOCAL7 - Reserved for local use
84	 *   LOG_LPR      - Line printer subsystem
85	 *   LOG_MAIL     - Mail subsystem
86	 *   LOG_NEWS     - USENET news subsystem
87	 *   LOG_SYSLOG   - Messages generated internally by syslogd(8)
88	 *   LOG_USER     - Generic user-level messages (default)
89	 *   LOG_UUCP     - UUCP subsystem
90	 */
91	
92	#define LOG_AUTH      0
93	#define LOG_AUTHPRIV  0
94	#define LOG_CRON      0
95	#define LOG_DAEMON    0
96	#define LOG_FTP       0
97	#define LOG_KERN      0
98	#define LOG_LOCAL0    0
99	#define LOG_LOCAL1    0
100	#define LOG_LOCAL2    0
101	#define LOG_LOCAL3    0
102	#define LOG_LOCAL4    0
103	#define LOG_LOCAL5    0
104	#define LOG_LOCAL6    0
105	#define LOG_LOCAL7    0
106	#define LOG_LPR       0
107	#define LOG_MAIL      0
108	#define LOG_NEWS      0
109	#define LOG_SYSLOG    0
110	#define LOG_USER      0
111	#define LOG_UUCP      0
112	
113	/* This determines the importance of the message. The levels are, in order
114	 * of decreasing importance:
115	 */
116	
117	#define LOG_EMERG     0  /* System is unusable */
118	#define LOG_ALERT     1  /* Action must be taken immediately */
119	#define LOG_CRIT      2  /* Critical conditions */
120	#define LOG_ERR       3  /* Error conditions */
121	#define LOG_WARNING   4  /* Warning conditions */
122	#define LOG_NOTICE    5  /* Normal, but significant, condition */
123	#define LOG_INFO      6  /* Informational message */
124	#define LOG_DEBUG     7  /* Debug-level message */
125	
126	/* Used with setlogmask() */
127	
128	#define LOG_MASK(p)   (1 << (p))
129	#define LOG_UPTO(p)   ((1 << ((p)+1)) - 1)
130	#define LOG_ALL       0xff

141	/****************************************************************************
142	 * Name: openlog
143	 *
144	 * Description:
145	 *   The openlog() function sets process attributes that affect subsequent
146	 *   calls to syslog(). The ident argument is a string that is prepended to
147	 *   every message. The logopt argument indicates logging options. Values
148	 *   for logopt are constructed by a bitwise-inclusive OR of zero or more of
149	 *   the following:
150	 *
151	 *     LOG_PID - Log the process ID with each message. This is useful for
152	 *       identifying specific processes.
153	 *
154	 *     LOG_CONS - Write messages to the system console if they cannot be
155	 *       sent to the logging facility. The syslog() function ensures that
156	 *       the process does not acquire the console as a controlling terminal
157	 *       in the process of writing the message.
158	 *
159	 *     LOG_NDELAY - Open the connection to the logging facility immediately.
160	 *       Normally the open is delayed until the first message is logged.
161	 *       This is useful for programs that need to manage the order in which
162	 *       file descriptors are allocated.
163	 *
164	 *     LOG_ODELAY - Delay open until syslog() is called.
165	 *
166	 *     LOG_NOWAIT - Do not wait for child processes that may have been
167	 *       created during the course of logging the message. This option
168	 *       should be used by processes that enable notification of child
169	 *       termination using SIGCHLD, since syslog() may otherwise block
170	 *       waiting for a child whose exit status has already been collected.
171	 *
172	 *   The facility argument encodes a default facility to be assigned to all
173	 *   messages that do not have an explicit facility already encoded. The
174	 *   initial default facility is LOG_USER.
175	 *
176	 *   It is not necessary to call openlog() prior to calling syslog().
177	 *
178	 ****************************************************************************/
179	
180	/* Not supported */
181	#define openlog(i, o, f) {(void)(i); (void)(o); (void)(f);}
182	
183	/****************************************************************************
184	 * Name: closelog
185	 *
186	 * Description:
187	 *   The openlog() and syslog() functions may allocate a file descriptor.
188	 *   The closelog() function will close any open file descriptors allocated
189	 *   by previous calls to openlog() or syslog().
190	 *
191	 ****************************************************************************/
192	
193	/* Not supported */
194	#define closelog()

205	 *   The NuttX implementation does not support any special formatting

208	 *   The function vsyslog() performs the same task as syslog() with the
209	 *   difference that it takes a set of arguments which have been obtained
210	 *   using the stdarg variable argument list macros.
211	 *
212	 ****************************************************************************/
213	
214	#ifndef CONFIG_SYSLOG_TO_SCHED_NOTE

275	/****************************************************************************
276	 * Name: setlogmask
277	 *
278	 * Description:
279	 *   The setlogmask() function sets the logmask and returns the previous
280	 *   mask. If the mask argument is 0, the current logmask is not modified.
281	 *
282	 *   The SYSLOG priorities are: LOG_EMERG, LOG_ALERT, LOG_CRIT, LOG_ERR,
283	 *   LOG_WARNING, LOG_NOTICE, LOG_INFO, and LOG_DEBUG.  The bit corresponding
284	 *   to a priority p is LOG_MASK(p); LOG_UPTO(p) provides the mask of all
285	 *   priorities in the above list up to and including p.
286	 *
287	 *   Per OpenGroup.org "If the maskpri argument is 0, the current log mask
288	 *   is not modified."  In this implementation, the value zero is permitted
289	 *   in order to disable all syslog levels.
290	 *
291	 *   NOTE:  setlogmask is not a thread-safe, re-entrant function.  Concurrent
292	 *   use of setlogmask() will have undefined behavior.
293	 *
294	 *   REVISIT: Per POSIX the syslog mask should be a per-process value but in
295	 *   NuttX, the scope of the mask is dependent on the nature of the build:
296	 *
297	 *   Flat Build:  There is one, global SYSLOG mask that controls all output.
298	 *   Protected Build:  There are two SYSLOG masks.  One within the kernel
299	 *     that controls only kernel output.  And one in user-space that controls
300	 *     only user SYSLOG output.
301	 *   Kernel Build:  The kernel build is compliant with the POSIX requirement:
302	 *     There will be one mask for for each user process, controlling the
303	 *     SYSLOG output only form that process.  There will be a separate mask
304	 *     accessible only in the kernel code to control kernel SYSLOG output.
305	 *
306	 ****************************************************************************/
307	
308	int setlogmask(int mask);
309	
310	#if defined(__cplusplus)
311	}
312	#endif

68	{
69	  SYSLOG_UNINITIALIZED = 0, /* SYSLOG has not been initialized */
70	  SYSLOG_INITIALIZING,      /* SYSLOG is being initialized */
71	  SYSLOG_REOPEN,            /* SYSLOG open failed... try again later */
72	  SYSLOG_FAILURE,           /* SYSLOG open failed... close and try again */
73	  SYSLOG_OPENED,            /* SYSLOG device is open and ready to use */
74	};

118	/****************************************************************************
119	 * Name: syslog_dev_open
120	 *
121	 * Description:
122	 *   Opens the SYSLOG character device (or file).
123	 *
124	 * Input Parameters:
125	 *   syslog_dev - Handle to syslog device to be used.
126	 *   devpath    - The full path to the character device to be used.
127	 *   oflags     - File open flags.
128	 *   mode       - File open mode (only if oflags include O_CREAT).
129	 *
130	 * Returned Value:
131	 *   Zero (OK) is returned on success; a negated errno value is returned on
132	 *   any failure.
133	 *
134	 ****************************************************************************/
135	
136	static int syslog_dev_open(FAR struct syslog_dev_s *syslog_dev,
137	                           FAR const char *devpath, int oflags, int mode)
138	{
139	  int ret;
140	
141	  /* At this point, the only expected states are SYSLOG_UNINITIALIZED or
142	   * SYSLOG_REOPEN.  Not SYSLOG_INITIALIZING, SYSLOG_FAILURE, SYSLOG_OPENED.
143	   */
144	
145	  DEBUGASSERT(syslog_dev->sl_state == SYSLOG_UNINITIALIZED ||
146	              syslog_dev->sl_state == SYSLOG_REOPEN);
147	
148	  /* Save the path to the device in case we have to re-open it.
149	   * If we get here and sl_devpath is not equal to NULL, that is a clue
150	   * that we are re-opening the file.
151	   */
152	
153	  if (syslog_dev->sl_state == SYSLOG_REOPEN)
154	    {
155	      /* Re-opening: Then we should already have a copy of the path to the
156	       * device. But that may be for a different device if we revert back
157	       * to old syslog destination after the previous attempt failed.
158	       */
159	
160	      DEBUGASSERT(syslog_dev->sl_devpath != NULL);
161	    }
162	  else
163	    {
164	      /* Initializing. We do not have the device path yet. */
165	
166	      DEBUGASSERT(syslog_dev->sl_devpath == NULL);
167	    }
168	
169	  /* Copy the device path so that we can use it if we
170	   * have to re-open the file.
171	   */
172	
173	  syslog_dev->sl_oflags = oflags;
174	  syslog_dev->sl_mode = mode;
175	  if (syslog_dev->sl_devpath != devpath)
176	    {
177	      if (syslog_dev->sl_devpath != NULL)
178	        {
179	          kmm_free(syslog_dev->sl_devpath);
180	        }
181	
182	      syslog_dev->sl_devpath = strdup(devpath);
183	    }
184	
185	  DEBUGASSERT(syslog_dev->sl_devpath != NULL);
186	
187	  syslog_dev->sl_state = SYSLOG_INITIALIZING;
188	
189	  /* Open the device driver. */
190	
191	  ret = file_open(&syslog_dev->sl_file, devpath, oflags, mode);
192	  if (ret < 0)
193	    {
194	      /* We failed to open the file. Perhaps it does exist?  Perhaps it
195	       * exists, but is not ready because it depends on insertion of a
196	       * removable device?
197	       *
198	       * In any case we will attempt to re-open the device repeatedly.
199	       * The assumption is that the device path is valid but that the
200	       * driver has not yet been registered or a removable device has
201	       * not yet been installed.
202	       */
203	
204	      syslog_dev->sl_state = SYSLOG_REOPEN;
205	      return ret;
206	    }
207	
208	  /* The SYSLOG device is open and ready for writing. */
209	
210	  syslog_dev->sl_state = SYSLOG_OPENED;
211	  return OK;
212	}

214	/****************************************************************************
215	 * Name: syslog_dev_outputready
216	 *
217	 * Description:
218	 * Ignore any output:
219	 *
220	 * (1) Before the SYSLOG device has been initialized.  This could happen
221	 *     from debug output that occurs early in the boot sequence before
222	 *     syslog_dev_initialize() is called (SYSLOG_UNINITIALIZED).
223	 * (2) While the device is being initialized.  The case could happen if
224	 *     debug output is generated while syslog_dev_initialize() executes
225	 *     (SYSLOG_INITIALIZING).
226	 * (3) While we are generating SYSLOG output.  The case could happen if
227	 *     debug output is generated while syslog_dev_putc() executes
228	 *     (This case is actually handled inside of syslog_lock()).
229	 * (4) Any debug output generated from interrupt handlers.  A disadvantage
230	 *     of using the generic character device for the SYSLOG is that it
231	 *     cannot handle debug output generated from interrupt level handlers.
232	 * (5) Any debug output generated from the IDLE loop.  The character
233	 *     driver interface is blocking and the IDLE thread is not permitted
234	 *     to block.
235	 * (6) If any failure occurred during output.  In this case, we properly
236	 *     close the device, and set it for later re-opening.
237	 *
238	 * NOTE: That the third case is different.  It applies only to the thread
239	 * that currently holds the sl_lock.  Other threads should wait.
240	 * that is why that case is handled in syslog_lock().
241	 *
242	 * Input Parameters:
243	 *   syslog_dev  - Handle to syslog device to be used.
244	 *
245	 * Returned Value:
246	 *   Zero (OK) is returned on success; a negated errno value is returned on
247	 *   any failure.
248	 *
249	 ****************************************************************************/
250	
251	static int syslog_dev_outputready(FAR struct syslog_dev_s *syslog_dev)
252	{
253	  int ret;
254	
255	  /* We can save checks in the usual case:  That after the SYSLOG device
256	   * has been successfully opened.
257	   */
258	
259	  if (syslog_dev->sl_state != SYSLOG_OPENED)
260	    {
261	      if (up_interrupt_context() || sched_idletask())
262	        {
263	          return -ENOSYS;
264	        }
265	
266	      /* Case (1) and (2) */
267	
268	      if (syslog_dev->sl_state == SYSLOG_UNINITIALIZED ||
269	          syslog_dev->sl_state == SYSLOG_INITIALIZING)
270	        {
271	          return -EAGAIN; /* Can't access the SYSLOG now... maybe next time? */
272	        }
273	
274	      /* Case (6) */
275	
276	      if (syslog_dev->sl_state == SYSLOG_FAILURE)
277	        {
278	          file_close(&syslog_dev->sl_file);
279	
280	          syslog_dev->sl_state = SYSLOG_REOPEN;
281	        }
282	
283	      /* syslog_dev_initialize() is called as soon as enough of the operating
284	       * system is in place to support the open operation... but it is
285	       * possible that the SYSLOG device is not yet registered at that time.
286	       * In this case, we know that the system is sufficiently initialized
287	       * to support an attempt to re-open the SYSLOG device.
288	       */
289	
290	      if (syslog_dev->sl_state == SYSLOG_REOPEN)
291	        {
292	          /* Try again to initialize the device.  We may do this repeatedly
293	           * because the log device might be something that was not ready
294	           * the first time that syslog_dev_initialize() was called (such as
295	           * a USB serial device that has not yet been connected or a file in
296	           * an NFS mounted file system that has not yet been mounted).
297	           */
298	
299	          DEBUGASSERT(syslog_dev->sl_devpath != NULL);
300	          ret = syslog_dev_open(syslog_dev, syslog_dev->sl_devpath,
301	                                (int)syslog_dev->sl_oflags,
302	                                (int)syslog_dev->sl_mode);
303	          if (ret < 0)
304	            {
305	              return ret;
306	            }
307	        }
308	
309	      DEBUGASSERT(syslog_dev->sl_state == SYSLOG_OPENED);
310	    }
311	
312	  return OK;
313	}

315	/****************************************************************************
316	 * Name: syslog_dev_write
317	 *
318	 * Description:
319	 *   This is the low-level, multiple byte, system logging interface provided
320	 *   for the character driver interface.
321	 *
322	 * Input Parameters:
323	 *   channel    - Handle to syslog channel to be used.
324	 *   buffer     - The buffer containing the data to be output.
325	 *   buflen     - The number of bytes in the buffer.
326	 *
327	 * Returned Value:
328	 *   On success, the character is echoed back to the caller. A negated errno
329	 *   value is returned on any failure.
330	 *
331	 ****************************************************************************/
332	
333	static ssize_t syslog_dev_write(FAR syslog_channel_t *channel,
334	                                FAR const char *buffer, size_t buflen)
335	{
336	  FAR struct syslog_dev_s *syslog_dev = (FAR struct syslog_dev_s *)channel;
337	  int ret;
338	
339	  /* Check if the system is ready to do output operations */
340	
341	  ret = syslog_dev_outputready(syslog_dev);
342	  if (ret < 0)
343	    {
344	      return ret;
345	    }
346	
347	  ret = file_write(&syslog_dev->sl_file, buffer, buflen);
348	  if (ret < 0)
349	    {
350	      syslog_dev->sl_state = SYSLOG_FAILURE;
351	    }
352	
353	  return ret;
354	}
355	
356	/****************************************************************************
357	 * Name: syslog_dev_putc
358	 *
359	 * Description:
360	 *   This is the low-level, single character, system logging interface
361	 *   provided for the character driver interface.
362	 *
363	 * Input Parameters:
364	 *   channel    - Handle to syslog channel to be used.
365	 *   ch         - The character to add to the SYSLOG (must be positive).
366	 *
367	 * Returned Value:
368	 *   On success, the character is echoed back to the caller. A negated errno
369	 *   value is returned on any failure.
370	 *
371	 ****************************************************************************/
372	
373	static int syslog_dev_putc(FAR syslog_channel_t *channel, int ch)
374	{
375	  FAR struct syslog_dev_s *syslog_dev = (FAR struct syslog_dev_s *)channel;
376	  ssize_t nbytes;
377	  uint8_t uch;
378	  int ret;
379	
380	  /* Check if the system is ready to do output operations */
381	
382	  ret = syslog_dev_outputready(syslog_dev);
383	  if (ret < 0)
384	    {
385	      return ret;
386	    }
387	
388	  uch = (uint8_t)ch;
389	  nbytes = file_write(&syslog_dev->sl_file, &uch, 1);
390	  if (nbytes < 0)
391	    {
392	      syslog_dev->sl_state = SYSLOG_FAILURE;
393	    }
394	
395	  return nbytes;
396	}

398	/****************************************************************************
399	 * Name: syslog_dev_flush
400	 *
401	 * Description:
402	 *   Flush any buffer data in the file system to media.
403	 *
404	 * Input Parameters:
405	 *   channel    - Handle to syslog channel to be used.
406	 *
407	 * Returned Value:
408	 *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
409	 *
410	 ****************************************************************************/
411	
412	static int syslog_dev_flush(FAR syslog_channel_t *channel)
413	{
414	#if defined(CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE) && !defined(CONFIG_DISABLE_MOUNTPOINT)
415	  FAR struct syslog_dev_s *syslog_dev = (FAR struct syslog_dev_s *)channel;
416	
417	  /* Ignore return value, always return success.  file_fsync() could fail
418	   * because the file is not open, the inode is not a mountpoint, or the
419	   * mountpoint does not support the sync() method.
420	   */
421	
422	  file_fsync(&syslog_dev->sl_file);
423	#else
424	  UNUSED(channel);
425	#endif
426	
427	  return OK;
428	}

434	/****************************************************************************
435	 * Name: syslog_dev_initialize
436	 *
437	 * Description:
438	 *   Initialize to use the character device (or file) at
439	 *   CONFIG_SYSLOG_DEVPATH as the SYSLOG sink.
440	 *
441	 *   On power up, the SYSLOG facility is non-existent or limited to very
442	 *   low-level output.  This function may be called later in the
443	 *   initialization sequence after full driver support has been initialized.
444	 *   (via syslog_initialize())  It installs the configured SYSLOG drivers
445	 *   and enables full SYSLOGing capability.
446	 *
447	 *   NOTE that this implementation excludes using a network connection as
448	 *   SYSLOG device.  That would be a good extension.
449	 *
450	 * Input Parameters:
451	 *   devpath - The full path to the character device to be used.
452	 *   oflags  - File open flags.
453	 *   mode    - File open mode (only if oflags include O_CREAT).
454	 *
455	 * Returned Value:
456	 *   Returns a newly created SYSLOG channel, or NULL in case of any failure.
457	 *
458	 ****************************************************************************/
459	
460	FAR syslog_channel_t *syslog_dev_initialize(FAR const char *devpath,
461	                                            int oflags, int mode)
462	{
463	  FAR struct syslog_dev_s *syslog_dev;
464	
465	  syslog_dev = kmm_zalloc(sizeof(struct syslog_dev_s));
466	
467	  if (syslog_dev == NULL)
468	    {
469	      return NULL;
470	    }
471	
472	  syslog_dev_open(syslog_dev, devpath, oflags, mode);
473	
474	  syslog_dev->sl_channel.sc_ops = &g_syslog_dev_ops;
475	
476	  return (FAR syslog_channel_t *)syslog_dev;
477	}

479	/****************************************************************************
480	 * Name: syslog_dev_uninitialize
481	 *
482	 * Description:
483	 *   Disable the last device/file channel in preparation to use a different
484	 *   SYSLOG device. Currently only used for CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE.
485	 *
486	 * Input Parameters:
487	 *   channel    - Handle to syslog channel to be used.
488	 *
489	 * Returned Value:
490	 *   Zero (OK) is returned on success; a negated errno value is returned on
491	 *   any failure.
492	 *
493	 * Assumptions:
494	 *   The caller has already switched the SYSLOG source to some safe channel
495	 *   (the default channel).
496	 *
497	 ****************************************************************************/
498	
499	void syslog_dev_uninitialize(FAR syslog_channel_t *channel)
500	{
501	  FAR struct syslog_dev_s *syslog_dev = (FAR struct syslog_dev_s *)channel;
502	
503	  /* Uninitializing a SYSLOG device should not take place within
504	   * interrupt context.
505	   */
506	
507	  if (up_interrupt_context() || sched_idletask())
508	    {
509	      DEBUGASSERT(!up_interrupt_context() && !sched_idletask());
510	      return;
511	    }
512	
513	  /* The device cannot be uninitialized while it is being
514	   * initialized simultaneously.
515	   */
516	
517	  DEBUGASSERT(syslog_dev->sl_state != SYSLOG_UNINITIALIZED &&
518	              syslog_dev->sl_state != SYSLOG_INITIALIZING);
519	
520	  /* Attempt to flush any buffered data. */
521	
522	  syslog_dev_flush(channel);
523	
524	  /* Close the detached file instance. */
525	
526	  if (syslog_dev->sl_state == SYSLOG_OPENED ||
527	      syslog_dev->sl_state == SYSLOG_FAILURE)
528	    {
529	      file_close(&syslog_dev->sl_file);
530	    }
531	
532	  /* Set the device in UNINITIALIZED state. */
533	
534	  syslog_dev->sl_state = SYSLOG_UNINITIALIZED;
535	
536	  /* Free the device path */
537	
538	  if (syslog_dev->sl_devpath != NULL)
539	    {
540	      lib_free(syslog_dev->sl_devpath);
541	    }
542	
543	  /* Free the channel structure */
544	
545	  kmm_free(syslog_dev);
546	}

548	/****************************************************************************
549	 * Name: syslog_dev_channel
550	 *
551	 * Description:
552	 *   Configure to use the character device at CONFIG_SYSLOG_DEVPATH as the
553	 *   SYSLOG channel.
554	 *
555	 *   This tiny function is simply a wrapper around syslog_dev_initialize()
556	 *   and syslog_channel_register().  It calls syslog_dev_initialize() to
557	 *   configure the character device at CONFIG_SYSLOG_DEVPATH then calls
558	 *   syslog_channel_register() to use that device as the SYSLOG output
559	 *   channel.
560	 *
561	 *   NOTE interrupt level SYSLOG output will be lost in this case unless
562	 *   the interrupt buffer is used.
563	 *
564	 * Input Parameters:
565	 *   None
566	 *
567	 * Returned Value:
568	 *   A pointer to the new SYSLOG channel; NULL is returned on any failure.
569	 *
570	 ****************************************************************************/
571	
572	FAR syslog_channel_t *syslog_dev_channel(FAR const char *devpath)
573	{
574	  FAR syslog_channel_t *dev_channel;
575	
576	  /* Initialize the character driver interface */
577	
578	  dev_channel = syslog_dev_initialize(devpath, SYSLOG_OFLAGS, SYSLOG_OMODE);
579	  if (dev_channel == NULL)
580	    {
581	      return NULL;
582	    }
583	
584	  /* Use the character driver as the SYSLOG channel */
585	
586	  if (syslog_channel_register(dev_channel) != OK)
587	    {
588	      syslog_dev_uninitialize(dev_channel);
589	      dev_channel = NULL;
590	    }
591	
592	  return dev_channel;
593	}

/* CONFIG_SYSLOG_INTBUFFER - Enables an interrupt buffer that will be used
 *   to serialize debug output from interrupt handlers.
 * CONFIG_SYSLOG_INTBUFSIZE - The size of the interrupt buffer in bytes.
 * CONFIG_SYSLOG_DEVPATH - The full path to the system logging device
 *
 * In addition, some SYSLOG device must also be enabled that will provide
 * the syslog output channel.  As of this writing, there are two SYSLOG
 * devices available:
 *
 *   1. A RAM SYSLOGing device that will log data into a circular buffer
 *      that can be dumped using the NSH dmesg command.  This device is
 *      described in the include/nuttx/syslog/ramlog.h header file.
 *
 *   2. And a generic character device that may be used as the SYSLOG.  The
 *      generic device interfaces are described in this file.  A disadvantage
 *      of using the generic character device for the SYSLOG is that it
 *      cannot handle debug output generated from interrupt level handlers.
 *
 * CONFIG_SYSLOG_CHAR - Enable the generic character device for the SYSLOG.
 *   The full path to the SYSLOG device is provided by CONFIG_SYSLOG_DEVPATH.
 *   A valid character device must exist at this path.  It will by opened
 *   by logic in syslog_initialize() based on the current configuration.
 *
 *   NOTE:  No more than one SYSLOG device should be configured.
 */

46	/****************************************************************************
47	 * Name: board_app_initialize
48	 *
49	 * Description:
50	 *   Perform application specific initialization.  This function is never
51	 *   called directly from application code, but only indirectly via the
52	 *   (non-standard) boardctl() interface using the command BOARDIOC_INIT.
53	 *
54	 *   CONFIG_BOARDCTL=y :
55	 *     Called from the NSH library
56	 *
57	 *   CONFIG_BOARD_LATE_INITIALIZE=y, CONFIG_NSH_LIBRARY=y, &&
58	 *   CONFIG_BOARDCTL=n :
59	 *     Called from board_late_initialize().
60	 *
61	 * Input Parameters:
62	 *   arg - The boardctl() argument is passed to the board_app_initialize()
63	 *         implementation without modification.  The argument has no
64	 *         meaning to NuttX; the meaning of the argument is a contract
65	 *         between the board-specific initialization logic and the
66	 *         matching application logic.  The value could be such things as a
67	 *         mode enumeration value, a set of DIP switch switch settings, a
68	 *         pointer to configuration data read from a file or serial FLASH,
69	 *         or whatever you would like to do with it.  Every implementation
70	 *         should accept zero/NULL as a default configuration.
71	 *
72	 * Returned Value:
73	 *   Zero (OK) is returned on success; a negated errno value is returned on
74	 *   any failure to indicate the nature of the failure.
75	 *
76	 ****************************************************************************/
77	
78	int board_app_initialize(uintptr_t arg)
79	{
80	  int ret;
81	
82	  /* Did we already initialize via board_late_initialize()? */
83	
84	#ifndef CONFIG_BOARD_LATE_INITIALIZE
85	  ret = stm32_bringup();
86	  if (ret < 0)
87	    {
88	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "ERROR: stm32_bringup() failed: %d\n", ret);
89	      return ret;
90	    }
91	#endif
92	
93	#ifdef CONFIG_CLICKER2_STM32_SYSLOG_FILE
94	
95	  /* Delay some time for the automounter to finish mounting before
96	   * bringing up file syslog.
97	   */
98	
99	  nxsig_usleep(CONFIG_CLICKER2_STM32_SYSLOG_FILE_DELAY * 1000);
100	
101	  syslog_channel_t *channel;
102	  channel = syslog_file_channel(CONFIG_CLICKER2_STM32_SYSLOG_FILE_PATH);
103	  if (channel == NULL)
104	    {
105	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "ERROR: syslog_file_channel() failed\n");
106	      return -EINVAL;
107	    }
108	#endif
109	
110	  UNUSED(ret);
111	  return OK;
112	}

NuttX 内核已内置了完整的 **`CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE`** 框架：



内置功能：

## 2. 推荐方案：Syslog File Channel（方案一）

### 2.1 架构图

```
 ┌──────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐
 │  app/vsyslog │ ──▶ │  syslog channel │ ──▶ │  /dev/console│  ◀── 原有（保留）
 │  kernel log  │     │  (multi-ch)     │     └──────────────┘
 └──────────────┘     │                 │     ┌──────────────┐
                      │                 │ ──▶ │ SD:/syslog/  │  ◀── 新增
                      └─────────────────┘     │  app.log     │
                                              └──────────────┘
```

**思路**：利用 `CONFIG_SYSLOG_MAX_CHANNELS` 支持多 channel，同时保留 console 输出（调试用）并新增 SD 卡文件输出（持久化）。

> 如果只需要 SD 卡输出（关闭 console），则不需要多 channel，更简单。

### 2.2 Kconfig 变更

```kconfig
# ====== 新增配置项 ======

# 启用 syslog 文件输出 channel
CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE=y

# 多 channel：console + file 双输出（可选，若只需文件则设 1）
CONFIG_SYSLOG_MAX_CHANNELS=2

# 日志轮转：保留 3 个历史文件
CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_ROTATIONS=3

# 单文件大小上限 512KB，超过则轮转
CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT=524288

# 重启后在文件末尾加分隔线，区分不同 boot session
CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_SEPARATE=y

# 中断上下文日志不丢失
CONFIG_SYSLOG_INTBUFFER=y
CONFIG_SYSLOG_INTBUFSIZE=1024

# 时间戳（已有 RTC + NTP）
CONFIG_SYSLOG_TIMESTAMP=y
CONFIG_SYSLOG_TIMESTAMP_REALTIME=y
CONFIG_SYSLOG_TIMESTAMP_FORMATTED=y
CONFIG_SYSLOG_TIMESTAMP_FORMAT="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"

# 日志前缀
CONFIG_SYSLOG_PRIORITY=y         # 显示级别 [INFO] [ERR] 等
CONFIG_SYSLOG_PROCESS_NAME=y     # 显示进程名
```

### 2.3 代码变更

**文件**：`board/esp32s3-touch-amoled/src/esp32s3_bringup.c`

在 `sdmmc_mount_task` 中，SD 卡挂载成功后，注册 syslog file channel：

```c
#ifdef CONFIG_ESP32S3_SDMMC

#include <nuttx/syslog/syslog.h>   /* 新增 */

#define SYSLOG_FILE_PATH  "/mnt/sd/syslog/app.log"

static int sdmmc_mount_task(int argc, FAR char *argv[])
{
  int ret;
  int mount_retries;
  struct stat buf;

  /* 创建挂载点 */
  ret = mkdir("/mnt", 0755);
  if (ret < 0 && errno != EEXIST)
    {
      syslog(LOG_ERR, "ERROR: Failed to create /mnt: %d\n", ret);
    }

  ret = mkdir("/mnt/sd", 0755);
  if (ret < 0 && errno != EEXIST)
    {
      syslog(LOG_ERR, "ERROR: Failed to create /mnt/sd: %d\n", ret);
    }

  /* SD 卡模式设置 */
  esp32s3_configgpio(17, OUTPUT);
  esp32s3_gpiowrite(17, true);
  usleep(10000);

  syslog(LOG_INFO, "Initializing SDMMC...\n");
  ret = board_sdmmc_initialize();
  if (ret < 0)
    {
      syslog(LOG_ERR, "ERROR: Failed to initialize SDMMC: %d\n", ret);
      return ret;   /* 新增：SD 卡不可用则提前退出 */
    }
  syslog(LOG_INFO, "SDMMC initialized successfully\n");

  /* 等待并挂载 SD 卡 */
  syslog(LOG_INFO, "Waiting for SD card...\n");
  for (mount_retries = 0; mount_retries < 20; mount_retries++)
    {
      if (stat("/dev/mmcsd1", &buf) == 0)
        {
          ret = nx_mount("/dev/mmcsd1", "/mnt/sd", "vfat", 0, NULL);
          if (ret == OK)
            {
              syslog(LOG_INFO, "SD card mounted at /mnt/sd\n");
              break;
            }
          syslog(LOG_ERR, "ERROR: Failed to mount SD card (attempt %d): %d\n",
                 mount_retries + 1, ret);
        }
      else
        {
          syslog(LOG_INFO, "SD card block device not ready (attempt %d)\n",
                 mount_retries + 1);
        }
      usleep(200000);
    }

  /* ====== 新增：Syslog 文件 Channel 注册 ====== */
#ifdef CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE
  /* 创建 syslog 目录 */
  ret = mkdir("/mnt/sd/syslog", 0755);
  if (ret < 0 && errno != EEXIST)
    {
      syslog(LOG_ERR, "ERROR: Failed to create syslog dir: %d\n", ret);
    }

  /* 将 syslog 重定向到 SD 卡上的文件 */
  FAR syslog_channel_t *file_ch;
  file_ch = syslog_file_channel(SYSLOG_FILE_PATH);
  if (file_ch == NULL)
    {
      syslog(LOG_ERR, "ERROR: syslog_file_channel() failed\n");
    }
  else
    {
      syslog(LOG_INFO, "Syslog file channel registered: %s\n",
             SYSLOG_FILE_PATH);
    }
#endif /* CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE */
  /* ====== 新增结束 ====== */

  return OK;
}
#endif /* CONFIG_ESP32S3_SDMMC */
```

### 2.4 多 Channel 共存（推荐完整方案）

如果希望 **console + SD 卡双输出**，启用多 channel：

```c
// syslog_channel_register() 会把 new channel 追加到 channel 数组，
// 不会替换已有的 console channel。
// 只要 CONFIG_SYSLOG_MAX_CHANNELS >= 2，两者共存。
```

Syslog 内部的工作机制：
- `syslog_write()` 遍历 `g_syslog_channel[]` 中所有已注册 channel
- 每条日志会同时写入 console 和 SD 卡文件

### 2.5 日志轮转效果

启用 `CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_ROTATIONS=3` 后，SD 卡上的文件结构：

```
/mnt/sd/syslog/
├── app.log        ← 当前日志文件
├── app.log.0      ← 上一个（最新历史）
├── app.log.1      ← 更早的
└── app.log.2      ← 最早的
```

每次 app.log 超过 512KB 时自动轮转，最老的文件被丢弃。

## 3. 备选方案

### 方案二：应用层文件写入（不推荐）

在应用代码中打开文件，手动 `fprintf` 写日志。不经过 syslog 框架。

**缺点**：
- 无法捕获内核/NuttX 框架层日志
- 中断上下文无法使用文件 I/O
- 需要自行处理缓冲、轮转、并发等
- 代码侵入性强

### 方案三：纯 RAMLOG + NSH dmesg 导出（轻量备选）

启用 `CONFIG_RAMLOG_SYSLOG=y`，日志写入内存环形缓冲区，通过 `dmesg > /mnt/sd/dmesg.txt` 定时导出。

**缺点**：
- RAMLOG 大小有限（默认 1024 字节，可适当增大）
- 需要定时任务主动导出，否则溢出丢失
- 非实时持久化，突然掉电丢失

**适用场景**：对 RAM 极度敏感的场合（方案一已经足够轻量，一般不需要）。

## 4. 关键技术要点

### 4.1 中断上下文日志保护

```
CONFIG_SYSLOG_INTBUFFER=y      # 必开
CONFIG_SYSLOG_INTBUFSIZE=1024  # 缓冲 1KB
```

SD 卡文件 I/O 不能在中断上下文执行。开启 interrupt buffer 后，中断中产生的日志先写入内存缓冲，待回到线程上下文时由 `syslog_flush_intbuffer()` 批量写入 SD 卡。

### 4.2 SD 卡插拔处理

`syslog_device.c` 的 `syslog_dev_outputready()` 已实现自动重连逻辑：

```
状态机: UNINITIALIZED → INITIALIZING → OPENED
                  ↑                      │
                  │      REOPEN ←── FAILURE
                  └────────┘
```

如果 SD 卡被拔出再插入，`file_write()` 失败后进入 `SYSLOG_FAILURE`，下次写入自动转为 `SYSLOG_REOPEN` 重新打开文件 — **对应用层透明**。

### 4.3 优雅关机

文件系统数据最终通过 `syslog_dev_flush()` 调用 `file_fsync()` 刷盘。建议在关机/重启前主动调用：

```c
syslog_flush();  // 强制刷盘所有 channel
```

或在 NSH 中添加关机脚本：
```bash
# /etc/rc.shutdown
echo "Shutting down, flushing logs..."
```

### 4.4 性能影响

| 指标 | 评估 |
|------|------|
| CPU 开销 | `file_write()` + FAT 层，非频繁日志可忽略；高频日志建议开 `SYSLOG_BUFFER` |
| SD 卡寿命 | 日志是顺序追加写入，FAT 文件系统元数据更新有限；轮转机制避免单文件过大 |
| 启动影响 | SD 卡挂载仍是异步任务，不阻塞 NSH 和 UI 启动 |

- Uses **standard NuttX syslog** (`syslog(LOG_ERR, ...)`, `syslog(LOG_INFO, ...)`) throughout the board bringup (`esp32s3_bringup.c`). This is the proper NuttX logging mechanism.

## 结论：直接使用 NuttX 内置的 `CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE`

NuttX 内核已自带完整的 syslog→文件 写入框架，几乎**不需要写新代码**，只需：

### 变更清单（3 处改动）

**1. Kconfig — 开启 `CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE` 及相关选项**

```ini
CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE=y              # 启用文件输出
CONFIG_SYSLOG_MAX_CHANNELS=2      # console + SD 卡双输出（单出可设1）
CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_ROTATIONS=3    # 保留3个历史文件
CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT=524288   # 单文件512KB后轮转
CONFIG_SYSLOG_INTBUFFER=y         # 中断日志保护
CONFIG_SYSLOG_INTBUFSIZE=1024
CONFIG_SYSLOG_TIMESTAMP=y         # 时间戳
CONFIG_SYSLOG_TIMESTAMP_REALTIME=y
CONFIG_SYSLOG_TIMESTAMP_FORMATTED=y
CONFIG_SYSLOG_PRIORITY=y          # 显示 [ERR]/[INFO] 级别
```

**2. `esp32s3_bringup.c` — SD 卡挂载后注册 file channel**

在 `sdmmc_mount_task()` 中 SD 卡 `nx_mount` 成功后加 7 行：

```c
#include <nuttx/syslog/syslog.h>

// ... SD mount success 之后 ...
#ifdef CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE
  mkdir("/mnt/sd/syslog", 0755);
  syslog_file_channel("/mnt/sd/syslog/app.log");
  // 之后所有 syslog()/printf() 输出自动写入该文件
#endif
```

**3. 无需改应用层代码** — 内核 syslog 框架透明接管所有 printf/syslog 输出。

### 关键特性（全是现成的）

| 特性 | 机制 |
|------|------|
| **SD 卡热插拔** | `syslog_device.c` 状态机自动 REOPEN，掉卡不丢数据 |
| **日志轮转** | 超大小自动 app.log → app.log.0 → app.log.1 |
| **中断安全** | `SYSLOG_INTBUFFER` 暂存中断日志，回线程后写入 |
| **掉电保护** | `syslog_dev_flush()` 主动 fsync，关机脚本再补一次 |
| **多通道共存** | `MAX_CHANNELS>=2` 同时写 console + SD 卡 |

## 方案总结

**一句话：开启 NuttX 内置 `CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE`，在 SD 卡挂载后调用 `syslog_file_channel("/mnt/sd/syslog/app.log")`，3 处改动即可完成。**

### 实现要点

| 层面 | 说明 |
|------|------|
| **Kconfig** | 开启 `SYSLOG_FILE` + `SYSLOG_FILE_ROTATIONS`（日志轮转）+ `SYSLOG_INTBUFFER`（中断保护）+ 时间戳 |
| **代码改动** | 仅在 `esp32s3_bringup.c` 的 `sdmmc_mount_task()` 中 SD 挂载成功后加一行 `syslog_file_channel()` 调用 |
| **应用层** | 零改动 — 所有 `syslog()`/`printf()` 输出透明写入 SD 卡 |
| **轮转效果** | 单文件超 512KB 自动轮转，保留 3 个历史文件，保持 `/mnt/sd/syslog/app.log` 始终为当前日志 |
| **SD 热插拔** | `syslog_device.c` 内置状态机自动重连，卡拔出后下次插入时自动恢复 |
| **中断安全** | 中断中产生的日志先入环形缓冲，回线程上下文后批量写 SD 卡 |
| **多通道并存** | `CONFIG_SYSLOG_MAX_CHANNELS=2` 同时输出 console + SD 卡 |

## 变更清单

### 文件 1：`board/esp32s3-touch-amoled/configs/openvela/defconfig`

| 新增项 | 作用 |
|--------|------|
| `CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE=y` | 启用文件输出通道 |
| `CONFIG_SYSLOG_MAX_CHANNELS=2` | console + SD 卡双通道 |
| `CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_ROTATIONS=3` | 保留 3 个历史日志文件 |
| `CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT=524288` | 单文件 512KB 触发轮转 |
| `CONFIG_SYSLOG_FILE_SEPARATE=y` | 重启时在日志文件加分隔线 |
| `CONFIG_SYSLOG_INTBUFFER=y` + `BUFSIZE=1024` | 中断上下文日志保护 |
| `CONFIG_SYSLOG_TIMESTAMP=y` + `FORMATTED` + `REALTIME` | 带格式的时间戳 |
| `CONFIG_SYSLOG_PRIORITY=y` | 显示 `[ERR]`/`[INFO]` 级别 |

| 修改项 | 旧值 | 新值 |
|--------|------|------|
| `SYSLOG_DEFAULT_MASK` | `0`（所有级别被过滤） | `0xff`（所有级别放行） |

385	/****************************************************************************
386	 * Name: syslog_channel
387	 *
388	 * Description:
389	 *   Configure the SYSLOGging function to use the provided channel to
390	 *   generate SYSLOG output.
391	 *
392	 * Input Parameters:
393	 *   channel - Provides the interface to the channel to be used.

397	 *   on any failure.

401	#ifdef CONFIG_SYSLOG_REGISTER
402	int syslog_channel_register(FAR syslog_channel_t *channel)
403	{
404	  DEBUGASSERT(channel != NULL);
405	
406	  if (channel != NULL)
407	    {
408	#if CONFIG_SYSLOG_MAX_CHANNELS == 1
409	      g_syslog_channel[0] = channel;
410	      return OK;
411	#else
412	      int i;
413	
414	      for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_SYSLOG_MAX_CHANNELS; i++)
415	        {
416	          if (g_syslog_channel[i] == NULL)
417	            {
418	#  ifdef CONFIG_SYSLOG_IOCTL
419	              if (channel->sc_name[0] == '\0')
420	                {
421	                  snprintf(channel->sc_name, sizeof(channel->sc_name),
422	                           "channel-%p", channel->sc_ops);
423	                }
424	#  endif
425	
426	              g_syslog_channel[i] = channel;
427	              return OK;
428	            }
429	          else if (g_syslog_channel[i] == channel)
430	            {
431	              return OK;
432	            }
433	        }
434	#endif
435	    }
436	
437	  return -EINVAL;
438	}

440	/****************************************************************************
441	 * Name: syslog_channel_unregister
442	 *
443	 * Description:
444	 *   Removes an already configured SYSLOG channel from the list of used
445	 *   channels.
446	 *
447	 * Input Parameters:
448	 *   channel - Provides the interface to the channel to be removed.
449	 *
450	 * Returned Value:
451	 *   Zero (OK) is returned on success.  A negated errno value is returned
452	 *   on any failure.
453	 *
454	 ****************************************************************************/
455	
456	int syslog_channel_unregister(FAR syslog_channel_t *channel)
457	{
458	  int i;
459	
460	  DEBUGASSERT(channel != NULL);
461	
462	  if (channel != NULL)
463	    {
464	      for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_SYSLOG_MAX_CHANNELS; i++)
465	        {
466	          if (g_syslog_channel[i] == channel)
467	            {
468	              /* Get the rest of the channels one position back
469	               * to ensure that there are no holes in the list.
470	               */
471	
472	              while (i < (CONFIG_SYSLOG_MAX_CHANNELS - 1) &&
473	                     g_syslog_channel[i + 1] != NULL)
474	                {
475	                  g_syslog_channel[i] = g_syslog_channel[i + 1];
476	                  i++;
477	                }
478	
479	              g_syslog_channel[i] = NULL;
480	
481	              /* The channel is now removed from the list and its driver
482	               * can be safely uninitialized.
483	               */
484	
485	              if (channel->sc_ops->sc_close)
486	                {
487	                  channel->sc_ops->sc_close(channel);
488	                }
489	
490	              return OK;
491	            }
492	        }
493	    }
494	
495	  return -EINVAL;
496	}

41	/****************************************************************************
42	 * Name: syslog_initialize
43	 *
44	 * Description:
45	 *   One power up, the SYSLOG facility is non-existent or limited to very
46	 *   low-level output.  This function is called later in the initialization
47	 *   sequence after full driver support has been initialized.  It installs
48	 *   the configured SYSLOG drivers and enables full SYSLOGing capability.
49	 *
50	 *   This function performs these basic operations:
51	 *
52	 *   - Initialize the SYSLOG device
53	 *   - Call syslog_channel_register() to begin using that device.
54	 *
55	 *   If CONFIG_ARCH_SYSLOG is selected, then the architecture-specifica
56	 *   logic will provide its own SYSLOG device initialize which must include
57	 *   as a minimum a call to syslog_channel_register() to use the device.
58	 *
59	 * Input Parameters:
60	 *  None
61	 *
62	 * Returned Value:
63	 *   Zero (OK) is returned on success; a negated errno value is returned on
64	 *   any failure.
65	 *
66	 ****************************************************************************/
67	
68	int syslog_initialize(void)
69	{
70	  int ret = OK;
71	
72	#ifdef CONFIG_SYSLOG_DEFAULT_PANIC_ONLY
73	  syslog_panic_notifier_register();
74	#endif
75	
76	#if defined(CONFIG_SYSLOG_CHAR)
77	  /* Enable use of a character device as the SYSLOG device */
78	
79	  syslog_dev_channel(CONFIG_SYSLOG_DEVPATH);
80	#elif defined(CONFIG_SYSLOG_CONSOLE)
81	  /* Use the console device as the SYSLOG device */
82	
83	  syslog_dev_channel("/dev/console");
84	#endif
85	
86	#ifdef CONFIG_RAMLOG_SYSLOG
87	  ramlog_syslog_register();
88	#endif
89	
90	#ifdef CONFIG_SYSLOG_CHARDEV
91	  syslog_register();
92	#endif
93	
94	#ifdef CONFIG_SYSLOG_RPMSG
95	  syslog_rpmsg_init();
96	#endif
97	
98	#ifdef CONFIG_SYSLOG_RPMSG_SERVER
99	  syslog_rpmsg_server_init();
100	#endif
101	
102	  return ret;
103	}

## 修复总结

### 根因

VFAT 文件系统在 NuttX 中为每个 `file` handle 维护独立的 **sector cache**。syslog file channel 写入的数据在 sector cache 中（`FFBUFF_DIRTY`），但未刷盘时其他 handle（如 `cat` 执行的 `open`）从磁盘读到的是旧状态 — 空文件。

### 修复

新增 `syslog_flush_task`（优先级 50，每 5 秒），调用 `syslog_flush()` → `syslog_dev_flush()` → `file_fsync()` → `fat_sync()` 将 dirty cache 刷入 SD 卡。

### 验证方法

重新编译烧录后，**等待 5 秒以上**让第一个 flush 周期执行，然后：

```bash
cat /mnt/sd/syslog/app.log
```

应该能看到 `[2026-08-10 19:15:04] [  INFO] Syslog file channel: /mnt/sd/syslog/app.log` 及之后的所有日志。

|------|------|
